source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-118: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 118 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume a multi-node GPU collective over a RoCE fabric; verify NIC/switch models, VLAN and priority mapping, MTU, routes, congestion-control settings, collective version, GPU/NIC placement, clocks, and background load before changing configuration. Model the path from verbs work requests and queue pairs through registered buffers, Ethernet routes, completions, retransmissions, PFC/ECN, timeouts, and any fallback transport.

Hypothesis: under a fixed workload, message-size distribution, topology, routes, software, and load, correcting the suspected priority, congestion, MTU, or route-symmetry fault lowers p95/p99 collective latency (ms) and timeout/retry rate while preserving bandwidth (GB/s) and application throughput (samples/s or tokens/s). Establish repeated baseline distributions, then change one variable in a canary. Measure application latency, GPU/NIC utilization, queue-pair completion and retry counters, ECN/PFC marks or pauses, drops, retransmits, link errors, and fallback-path use with synchronized timestamps; report sample counts, percentiles, units, and confidence intervals.

Separate correlation from mechanism: a clean NIC counter or successful collective does not prove the intended path is healthy. Confounders include clock skew, incast, competing traffic, message mix, thermal throttling, placement, and library algorithm selection. Do not claim improvement without topology/config snapshots and packet/counter evidence. Stop and restore the last known-good configuration if p99, timeout rate, drops, or application errors breach the predeclared gate, or if PFC storms/link errors increase; isolate the canary and avoid unbounded retries. Evidence required: reproducible before/after runs, route and priority maps, NIC/switch counters, workload and software versions, and a controlled fallback comparison.

source_user: Advanced cluster case GDR-1: Design a validation plan for GPUDirect RDMA between GPUs and NICs. Variant 1 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: verify topology and peer access, registration and pinning, IOMMU/container permissions, NIC-GPU affinity, direct versus staged copies, and compare bandwidth and CPU utilization. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume a supported GPU, NIC, driver, CUDA, and container stack, and treat GPUDirect RDMA as a claim to validate rather than infer from a successful transfer. First capture GPU/NIC PCIe topology, peer-access capability, NUMA and NIC-GPU affinity, driver and firmware versions, IOMMU mode, container privileges, ACS/PCIe settings, and whether the memory is device memory. Verify registration and pinning behavior, address/lifetime rules, queue and completion semantics, and that the measured path is direct GPU memory to NIC DMA rather than a host-staged copy.

Hypothesis: for the same GPU/NIC pair, message sizes, direction, concurrency, NUMA placement, and software, enabling the intended GPUDirect path increases effective bandwidth (GB/s) and lowers CPU utilization (%) and transfer latency (us or ms) versus an explicitly staged-copy control, without increasing errors or tail latency. Establish repeated warm-up and steady-state baselines across small and large messages; measure end-to-end latency, bandwidth, p50/p95/p99, CPU cycles/utilization, GPU activity, PCIe/NIC counters, registration time, completion errors, retries, and host-memory traffic. Record units, sample counts, confidence intervals, topology, and configuration.

Use matched direct and staged controls and distinguish measured facts from estimates. Confounders include NUMA placement, PCIe link width/speed, IOMMU translation, registration cache effects, synchronization, contention, message size, GPU clocks, and hidden fallback. A transfer succeeding does not establish directness. Require profiler/trace or counter evidence of GPU DMA and no host staging. Stop the canary and roll back to the last known-good path if completion errors, data corruption, link errors, hangs, timeouts, or p99/CPU utilization exceed predeclared limits; preserve logs and do not retry indefinitely. Evidence required: topology and permissions, versions, directness trace, matched benchmark results, error/link counters, and reproducible workload details.
